title: Acanthamoeba Keratitis: The Sight-Threatening Paradox
summary: Acanthamoeba keratitis (AK) is a severe, potentially blinding protozoan infection of the cornea, characterized by intense pain disproportionate to clinical findings. Early detection is the cornerstone of visual preservation, as delayed diagnosis often leads to ring infiltrate formation and scleritis.

sections.title: Definition & Epidemiology
sections.content: Acanthamoeba is a free-living, ubiquitous protozoan (cysts and trophozoites) found in water, soil, and dust. AK is primarily associated with contact lens wear (85-90% of cases). Prevalence is rising due to increased soft contact lens (SCL) usage and improper hygiene, such as tap water rinsing or swimming in lenses.

branches: Trophozoite: Active, mobile, feeds on bacteria/corneal epithelial cells
Encystment: Dormant state, highly resistant to chlorine/anti-amoebic drugs
Adhesion: Mannose-binding protein facilitates corneal binding
Proteolysis: Secretion of collagenases/serine proteases inducing stromal necrosis

sections.title: Red Flags: Diagnostic Pitfalls
content: Pain disproportionate to slit-lamp signs (The 'Classic' mismatch)
Failure to respond to antibiotic or antiviral therapy
Ring infiltrate (usually a sign of late-stage disease)
Diagnostic delay exceeding 2-3 weeks significantly worsens prognosis

sections.title: Diagnostic Workup Protocol
content: Step 1: Corneal scraping (Gold standard) - Non-nutrient agar with E. coli overlay.
Step 2: In-vivo Confocal Microscopy (IVCM) - Visualizing double-walled cysts in vivo.
Step 3: PCR for Acanthamoeba DNA - Highly sensitive (up to 95%).
Step 4: Histopathology (if penetrating keratoplasty is performed) - Calcofluor white staining.

rows: Dendritic ulcers, positive history of recurrence

sections.title: Treatment Protocol
content: Adjuncts: Topical NSAIDs (for pain control), Cycloplegics (Atropine 1%).
Systemic: Oral Itraconazole may be considered in refractory cases.
Duration: Minimum 6-12 months of topical therapy to clear encysted forms.

sections.title: Memory Aid: The 3 R's of AK

content.explanation: Radiating pain (disproportionate), Radial keratoneuritis (nerve inflammation), Ring infiltrate (classic stromal ring).

sections.title: Key Clinical Pearls
content: Always suspect AK in contact lens wearers with persistent red eye.
Stop all contact lens wear immediately.
Avoid topical steroids early in the disease; they promote trophozoite transformation and proliferation.
Surgical intervention (PKP) is only for non-responsive cases/perforation due to high recurrence rates in inflamed tissue.
